execution.description: Battery's Track A family engine extracted into a Challenge-neutral attack engine with an adapter interface per Challenge and construction level, run end to end on a synthetic second Challenge at Levels 0 and 1.

expected: The engine moves out of battery's harness without changing a byte of battery's Track A records or report, and a second Challenge runs through it with no battery code.
observed: Hashing the harness's three outputs on the base commit before editing, twice, gave a deterministic pin; after the extraction they matched. The legacy family state read a family with no attempt, or without a control, as IN_PROGRESS, which is a vacuous pass; the engine reads it INCONCLUSIVE, and battery's real families are unaffected. A control evaluated through a boundary that only reports breaches cannot detect a wrongful refusal, so a control now needs the boundary's boolean accepted or its own check. The climb harness refuses Level 0 plans, so permission ablation is run from Level 1 and cited at Level 0. The reuse branch's suite coverage report ran on a branch commit outside main's history; it was kept verbatim with its provenance rather than presented as a fresh run.
keep: Pin an extracted component's outputs by hash on the base commit before editing it, and run the pin twice to confirm it is deterministic.
Prove neutrality with a synthetic second Challenge that supplies only the adapter interface, and with a source scan that the core names no Challenge.
Make no-evidence states (no attempt, no control, a silent specimen, no answer) INCONCLUSIVE, never a pass.
change: Re-run the suite v1 coverage for battery on main in the canonical lane, with all five dependency groups, before citing it as current evidence.
Give each adapter held-out controls at the family's edge, so wrongful rejection is measured where a boundary is most likely too narrow.
